pr_body:
Fixes #96768 

A fix proposal based on the [identified root cause](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/96768#issuecomment-1609907429).

The problem in general is that mapping properties parsing is affected by the `subobjects` setting, so if multiple mappings are merged, whenever explicit `subobjects` setting is encountered, formerly parsed mappings become invalid.
What I tried in this PR is to determine whether there is an explicit `subobjects` setting within a list of mappings before parsing (and merging) them. This allows for consistent parsing and merging of component templates when processing and validating composable component templates.

If this fix proposal is evaluated as a valid path, we still need to add some unit tests, for example:
- [x] different order of components in the `composedOf` list
- [x] contradicting `subobjects` settings
- [x] comparing the new bulk merge to the existing sequential merge
pr_comments: Hi @eyalkoren, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Does this fix the case when we have conflicting `subobjects` directives on a submapper (ie not directly on the root)?

I worry a bit that this is a special-case fix for one specific type of possible conflict, and that maybe we need to take a step back and see if there is a better way of doing this more generally.  In particular, it might be worth trying to merge the templates as json maps rather than as parsed mappings?  As I understand it, v2 templates are supposed to be parseable so that they can be verified when PUT, but I don't think that necessarily means that we need to merge them together as mappings at index creation time.

I think it might also be worth getting some input from @elastic/es-data-management given that they own the template code.

Summarizing my offline discussion with @romseygeek: we may be able to generically solve this problem by merging mappings in their raw form first, before parsing them, as in [`XContentHelper#mergeDefaults`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/84089fe7e490ff80e08ecfbf6815763ffa84fc5b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/xcontent/XContentHelper.java#L414), possibly with slight changes and only for merges during the composition of index templates.
One possible change we'd need to apply for the current merge for example- we may be OK with simply overriding the value for a field's "type" by another type coming from another mapping, but the current expectation is to not allow conflicts of field type with object type.

Another alternative is to postpone the object expansion based on `.` in field names to be done as late as possible, after merging is done, at which time we already have the full picture from all mappings. This may be much more complicated to do.

@dakrone your input on this would be very helpful.

Update (for my future self mostly): I added a test with the exact example described [above](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97317#issuecomment-1663592849) that fails as expected. 
Applying @romseygeek's proposal of merging the raw (non-parsed JSON `Map<String, Object>` representations) mappings through `XContentHelper#mergeDefaults` fixes the test. I already know it would fail other tests that expect merge exceptions when trying to merge field X with `type: object` with another mapping in which field X is mapped to a non-object type. 
So this approach seems valid so far, but we'd need to implement our own raw merge that is very similar to `mergeDefaults` but contains all special cases for mappings merges for index templates.

> I already know it would fail other tests that expect merge exceptions when trying to merge field X with type: object with another mapping in which field X is mapped to a non-object type.

I think it's likely that we'll still get exceptions, it's just that they'll be different exceptions?  For example, overriding an object mapper with a float mapper will then throw an exception at parse time, because float mappers can't have a `properties` subfield.

> I think it's likely that we'll still get exceptions, it's just that they'll be different exceptions? For example, overriding an object mapper with a float mapper will then throw an exception at parse time, because float mappers can't have a properties subfield.

It will then depend in the order of the merge. `XContentHelper#mergeDefaults` simply merges without knowing anything about what it is merging, so it doesn't know that it merges mappings and that the `type` key may require special handling or validations. 
When I ran `MetadataIndexTemplateServiceTests`, [`testIndexTemplateFailsToOverrideComponentTemplateMappingField()`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/ac68e54e8e6730cb0e7e323cd30338923d8edd8a/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/MetadataIndexTemplateServiceTests.java#L1840-L1843) failed because it expected an exception during validation, which did not occur because the merged raw map contained `type: object`, which is OK with `properties`. On the other hand, [`testUpdateComponentTemplateFailsIfResolvedIndexTemplatesWouldBeInvalid()`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/ac68e54e8e6730cb0e7e323cd30338923d8edd8a/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/MetadataIndexTemplateServiceTests.java#L1965-L1968) failed due to a different exception, where a `text` field is not expected to have `properties` subfield, as you say.

The point is that it is not so much about how tests will fail, but that we'll have to reproduce the same behavior in raw mapping merge as we get with parsed mappings merge.

Piping in here with some background. We originally designed the mappings merging to treat each field as a unit, where the unit would override the entire field definition, rather than merging it like a recursive json map merge. The idea was that by doing this we would avoid a situation where a user configures a field A with option X, Y, and Z and then has a different template with the same field A configured with option M, and N — we didn't want to end up with a field A with options X, Y, Z, M, and N, but only the highest precedence "unit" configuration for the field.

@dakrone thanks a lot for explaining the rationale 🙏 

One way to address the issue you raise is by defining what a _unit_ is and adjust the customized merge accordingly. For example, our customized merge can decide that under a node called `properties`, subtrees are _replaced_ instead of being _merged_. This maintains the exact unit semantics that you describe for fields.

The main question I need to be answered now is whether we should proceed with this direction and fix whatever needs fixing within the proposed merge, or should we abandon this path and do something else.
For example- instead of fixing the merge, we can fix the parsing logic by treating dots as a valid character for field names and stop relying on them to deduce object nesting.

If you want me to go down the current path, please provide all such limitations and scenarios and I'll adjust the algorithm accordingly.

> whether we should proceed with this direction and fix whatever needs fixing within the proposed merge, or should we abandon this path and do something else.
> For example- instead of fixing the merge, we can fix the parsing logic by treating dots as a valid character for field names and stop relying on them to deduce object nesting.

The field name parsing code is not an area with which I'm intimately familiar, so I'd defer this decision to @romseygeek and his team. As long as the merging invariant of "_two separate and valid mappings configurations of the same field name should always merge to a valid mapping configuration for the field_", then I think either approach is fine.

I finally got to actually look and there is indeed a [test case](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bac320829ca1385bcda70f70e5124570b513bf9e/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/MapperServiceTests.java#L1150-L1239) I added for it, but maybe yours is a specific scenario that is not properly covered.
Once I get to it, I'll test myself, but if you get the chance to verify as I asked, it would be useful.

issue_context.title: Composable template fails with `subobjects: false` and mappings in different component templates
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.9.0

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

macOS

### Problem Description

When trying to merge two component templates, one which contains explicit mappings for dotted fields and the other containing `subobjects: false`, composition fails with:
```
type: "mapper_parsing_exception"
reason: "Tried to add subobject [XXX] to object [_doc] which does not support subobjects"
```

If the `subobjects: false` is located within the same component template alongside the fields mappings- the error doesn't occur. 
Also, this error doesn't occur if the field mapping is made for a non-dotted field.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run this test through the yaml test framework:
```yml
  - do:
      cluster.put_component_template:
        name: test-subobjects
        body:
          template:
            mappings:
              subobjects: false

  - do:
      cluster.put_component_template:
        name: test-field
        body:
          template:
            mappings:
              properties:
                parent.subfield:
                  type: keyword

  - do:
      indices.put_index_template:
        name: logs-composable-template
        body:
          index_patterns:
            - test-*
          composed_of:
            - test-subobjects
            - test-field
```

NOTE:
- if `subobjects: false` is moved to be alongside the explicit mappings within the same component template - the error doesn't occur
- if the mapping is defined for the field `parent` and not `parent.subfield` - the error doesn't occur

review_comments: Nit: remove this and replace with the `_routing` field requirement

No, this is still true and it is the actual fix for the originally identified issue- we need to keep `subobjects` when we merge field mappings (e.g. of two `object` field definitions).
The `_routing` is [something else](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97317/files#diff-5081302eb39033199deb1977d544d1cd7867212a92b8d77e0aa0ded361272b11R101-R103), I will add another comment into the algorithm implementation in the right place.
Ah, I was misreading and thinking this was the conflict error part that we removed earlier.  All good then!

Note for reviewer: note that I had to use `"_routing": {"required": false}` explicitly here, instead of relying on the default, because otherwise there is no way to detect contradiction between mapping and settings coming from `ComposableIndexTemplate.DataStreamTemplate`, as they both get translated into a single `RoutingFieldMapper`.
Since this code is executed only if `template.getDataStreamTemplate() != null`, it should be same

This tests the mismatch between routing settings and routing enablement through `ComposableIndexTemplate.DataStreamTemplate`. In addition, I had to test conflicting `routing` configurations if such come from the mappings and a contradicting one comes from `ComposableIndexTemplate.DataStreamTemplate` (below).
This line doesn't need to be within the synchronized block I think?

Yeah, it's misleading in this sense 🙂 
It is currently within the synchronized block and [I learned the hard way](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97199#discussion_r1249541239) that it does need to stay in it.
Can you add a javadoc for a high-level explanation of how this custom merger behaves? I.e., its special treatment of `subobjects`, etc.
I think this needs a comment as to why this is necessary
I [commented](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97317/files#r1285950199) elsewhere about this in the PR. Did you mean that, or adding a comment to the code?
I meant in the code, so that future code spelunkers know why it's there.

Now the merge happens in the raw form of the mappings, which means that the parsing happens on **the superset of all mappings of each field**. So the test would fail a bit earlier than it was failing before, when it sees `type: keyword` and `ignore_malformed` together (`keyword` does not support `ignore_malformed`) for the `@timestamp` field. 
Changing the type to `long` restores the former expected failure of using wrong type for `@timestamp`.
Conceptually, this doesn't indicate a problem as it can only happen in invalid mappings combinations.

**Note for reviewer:** only the `XContentHelper.convertToMap()` operation was extracted from the formerly `synchronized` block. As far as I can see this is a stateless operation, which leaves the former synchronization enforcement the same.
Could we also add a test that does the merging for nested maps without a custom merge present? I think that's the only case missing right now?
